frontier.hypothesis: A duplication spelling exists that satisfies all three requirements at once - it duplicates the two func_80032854 calls (for the nrefs(arg1) dial), keeps the `<` arm's inner branch inverted (so jump2 merges only the call tail, leaving target's 4-insn arm), and keeps a live label between the `sh $v0,0x286($s0)` store and the `addiu $a1,$zero,1` argument set-up (so the store does not sink into the jal delay slot). That spelling is 215 insns at a floor below 20.
frontier.mechanism: Measured this session: R4/R5 satisfy (a) but not (b), so the arm fully merges and 3 instructions vanish; R6/R7 satisfy (a) and (b) but not (c), so the store sinks and 4-7 instructions appear. All three score 20, which means the two losses are worth the same and neither has been eliminated - the requirements are independent, not a trade-off. The store is pinned in the s9 body purely because the `<` arm's `goto do_calls;` keeps that label alive; the sink itself is the scheduler moving the store past the argument set-up into the jal's delay slot (the inverse of .claude/rules/defer-store-past-later-compute-into-jal-delay).
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate spellings that keep a THIRD entry into the shared block so the `do_calls` label survives while the calls are still duplicated - e.g. duplicate the pair into the `temp_v1_3 == 0` / `> 0` path instead of the `<` arm (that path currently owns the shared block, so the `<` arm would keep its `goto do_calls;` and both labels stay live), or split the `<` arm so its 0x19 branch gotos and its 0xB branch duplicates while a fourth site re-enters at `do_calls`. Measure each with `sandbox --disable all` and confirm with tools/ra_solver/extract.py that nrefs_flow(73) stays >= 8; the seat flip is only retained while it does.

frontier.hypothesis: Cluster B (the nop-vs-`li v0,1` divergence at emitted slots 45/47) and the frontier-1 reorg residual are ONE delay-slot-fill mechanism, not two.
frontier.mechanism: s10 proved cluster B does not move under any of the sixteen exit-form assignments, and this session's diff shows its exact shape: ours fills the last `beq $v1,$v0` of the dispatch chain's delay slot with `li $v0,1` and leaves the following `j`'s slot empty, while target does the reverse (nop in the beq slot, `li $v0,1` in the j's). That is reorg stealing across the .L80028488 label in our build and declining to in target's - the same class of decision as the frontier-1 `mark_target_live_regs` / opposite_needed loss that s10 measured at insn 344.
frontier.next_probe: Locate the dispatch chain's final `beq` insn UID in tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s10/iso_dumps/iso.dbr, grep that UID in tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s10/iso_dumps/dbr.log for its `thr`/`simp` lines, and check whether the steal is granted there for the same reason it is refused at 344. If both are opposite_needed decisions, clusters B and the frontier-1 nop collapse into one residual with one mechanism, and the s10 open sub-question (why v0 is in opposite_needed at insn 686 despite the REG_DEAD flush at label 347) becomes the single highest-value probe left on this function.
